correctness.rationale: For hub-containing connected starts, every seeded blade must have <=k white vertices and total order of entirely empty blades <=k; these necessary conditions are sufficient by explicit staged forcing. For hub-free connected starts, all seeds lie in one clique and exact first-force and residual-hub inequalities characterize success. Disjoint cases give the stated polynomial and all homogeneous thresholds including k=m,(r-1)m,rm. Independent graph-process enumeration verified 671 parameter tuples and 1,458,592 subsets.

Exhaustive actual published-finding corpus searches and specific primary-source comparisons found no mathematically dominating statement. value.rationale: The earliest directly matching 2020 paper established only the scalar connected k-forcing minimum for friendship graphs. The full polynomial for arbitrary heterogeneous clique bouquets records feasible connected seeds at every budget, including an exact empty-blade knapsack constraint. Its uniform special case yields all optimum multiplicities and an exact two-unit threshold drop, providing motivated reliability/cost information absent from the scalar invariant. This is a natural complete classification rather than a routine numerical increment.
